# Node reference

**36 nodes**, of which **19 are callable by an agent node as tools**.

This page is generated from the registry itself, so it cannot drift from what the product does.
Every entry below is one object in [`src/lib/nodes/`](../src/lib/nodes) — the same object the
engine dispatches through, the canvas palette renders, and the agent is handed as a tool
definition. See [`architecture.md`](./architecture.md) → *The registry is the spine*.

## Trigger

Every workflow starts at exactly one of these. Nothing may draw an edge into a trigger.

### `core.manual_trigger` — Manual trigger

**trigger** · **not** callable by the agent

Starts the workflow when somebody presses Run, with whatever you hand it as the first node's input. Declare fields and the canvas asks for them with a form — a required field that is missing stops the run before anything else happens.

**Input.** the values typed into the run form, or JSON sent with the run

**Output.** whatever JSON the run was started with. Reach its fields with {{trigger.<field>}}.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | array of object | no | `[]` |

**Examples**

- *Ask for a topic and an audience* — fields: [{ name: "topic", type: "text", required: true }, { name: "audience", type: "text" }] — then {{trigger.topic}}

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Starts the workflow when a person runs it. Any JSON supplied at trigger time becomes the output of this node.

</details>

### `core.webhook_trigger` — Webhook trigger

**trigger** · **not** callable by the agent

Starts the workflow when an external service POSTs JSON to this workflow's unique webhook URL. The posted JSON body becomes the output of this node. Use it when the request says the workflow starts from an incoming call, a form submission, or another system's event.

**Output.** the JSON object that was POSTed. Reach its fields with {{trigger.<field>}}, e.g. {{trigger.message}}.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requiredFields` | array of string | no | `[]` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Starts the workflow when an external service POSTs JSON to this workflow's unique webhook URL. The posted JSON body becomes the output of this node. Use it when the request says the workflow starts from an incoming call, a form submission, or another system's event.

</details>

### `core.schedule_trigger` — Schedule trigger

**trigger** · **not** callable by the agent

Starts the workflow on a repeating schedule, given as a 5-field cron expression in UTC (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Examples: "0 9 * * 1-5" is 09:00 UTC on weekdays, "*/30 * * * *" is every 30 minutes, "@daily" is midnight UTC. Use it when the request says the workflow runs every day, every hour, on a timetable, or at a particular time.

**Output.** { firedAt: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, cron: the expression, scheduledFor: the slot it fired for }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cron` | string | no | `0 9 * * *` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Starts the workflow on a repeating schedule, given as a 5-field cron expression in UTC (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Examples: "0 9 * * 1-5" is 09:00 UTC on weekdays, "*/30 * * * *" is every 30 minutes, "@daily" is midnight UTC. Use it when the request says the workflow runs every day, every hour, on a timetable, or at a particular time.

</details>

### `core.error_trigger` — Error trigger

**trigger** · **not** callable by the agent

Runs this workflow whenever another workflow in this workspace fails with nobody watching — not one somebody pressed Run on. Put a Slack, Discord or Gmail step after it and you have a failure alert. Press Run here to try it with a sample failure.

**Input.** nothing to configure — it fires for every workflow in the workspace you can see

**Output.** { workflow: { id, name }, run: { id, trigger, startedAt, url }, failedStep: { id, label, type } or null, error }, e.g. {{trigger.workflow.name}}, {{trigger.error}}, {{trigger.run.url}}.

_No configuration._

**Examples**

- *Post failures to Discord* — "{{trigger.workflow.name}} failed at {{trigger.failedStep.label}}: {{trigger.error}} — {{trigger.run.url}}"
- *Only one workflow* — Follow it with a Branch: {{trigger.workflow.name}} equals Invoice sync

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Starts the workflow when another workflow here fails while running by itself, with nobody watching. Use it to alert on failures: follow it with a Slack, Discord or Gmail node.

</details>

### `core.form_trigger` — Form trigger

**trigger** · **not** callable by the agent

A web page anyone with the link can fill in — no sign-in. Add the fields you want (a name, a label, a type, whether it is required) and each answer becomes a value your steps can use. The link is secret and can be replaced from the trigger's panel. Add a Respond step to change what the visitor is told.

**Input.** nothing — it starts the run. Field names are what you reach as {{trigger.name}}

**Output.** an object with one key per field, e.g. {{trigger.email}}. A checkbox is true or false; a number is a number.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | no | `""` |
| `description` | string | no | `""` |
| `fields` | array of object | no | `[]` |
| `submitLabel` | string | no | `Submit` |
| `successMessage` | string | no | `Thanks — your response was received.` |
| `failureMessage` | string | no | `Something went wrong, and your response may not have been received. Please try again in a moment.` |

**Examples**

- *A field's answer* — {{trigger.email}}
- *A field set up as a choice* — name: plan · type: select · options: "Free, Team, Enterprise"
- *Tell the visitor something specific* — Add a Respond step with status 200 and body message: Thanks {{trigger.name}}

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Starts the workflow when someone submits a hosted web form. Use it when the request says a form, a sign-up, a survey or a contact page. Declare "fields": a list of { "name": "email", "label": "Your email", "type": text|longtext|email|number|select|checkbox|date, "required": true, "options": "A, B, C" (select only) }. Each answer is then {{trigger.<name>}}.

</details>

## Logic

Flow control and plumbing — the nodes that decide where a run goes next, or pause it.

### `core.log` — Log message

**action** · callable by the agent

Writes a message to the run log and passes its input through unchanged. Use it to record what happened at a point in the workflow.

**Output.** its input, unchanged.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | no | `""` |
| `level` | `info` · `warn` · `error` | no | `info` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Writes a message to the run log and passes its input through unchanged. Use it to record what happened at a point in the workflow.

</details>

### `core.branch` — Branch

**branch** · **not** callable by the agent

Compares two values and sends the run down the 'true' or 'false' output. Values usually reference earlier data, e.g. left = {{input.status}}, operator = equals, right = ok.

**Output.** { matched: true or false — which output was taken, input: the data that came in, passed through }.

**Branches.** True (`true`) · False (`false`)

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `left` | any | yes | — |
| `operator` | `equals` · `not_equals` · `contains` · `greater_than` · `less_than` · `is_empty` · `is_not_empty` | no | `equals` |
| `right` | any | no | — |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Compares two values and sends the run down the 'true' or 'false' output. Values usually reference earlier data, e.g. left = {{input.status}}, operator = equals, right = ok.

</details>

### `core.switch` — Switch

**branch** · **not** callable by the agent

Sends the run one of five ways depending on a value. Cases are tested top to bottom and the first match wins, so put the most specific case first. Anything that matches nothing leaves through 'Otherwise'.

**Input.** Nothing — it tests the `value` you configure, which is usually a `{{ }}` reference.

**Output.** { matched: the 1-based case number or null, branch: the output taken, value: what was tested }.

**Branches.** Case 1 (`1`) · Case 2 (`2`) · Case 3 (`3`) · Case 4 (`4`) · Otherwise (`else`)

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | any | yes | — |
| `cases` | array of object | no | `[]` |

**Examples**

- *Route by priority* — value: {{input.priority}} · case 1 equals "urgent" · case 2 equals "high" · else → the normal path
- *Route by size* — value: {{steps.count.output.value}} · case 1 greater_than 100 · case 2 greater_than 10

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Routes the run down one of four outputs by testing a value against each case in order, or down the 'else' output when none match. Use it instead of chaining Branch nodes when a value has several possible destinations.

</details>

### `core.loop` — Loop

**loop** · **not** callable by the agent

Repeats the nodes connected to its 'loop' output once per item, then continues from its 'done' output. Iterates the incoming array, or the configured items, up to maxIterations. The number of iterations is always bounded.

**Output.** on the loop output, { index, item, total } for the current item; on the done output, { done: true, iterations, items }.

**Branches.** Each item (`loop`) · Done (`done`)

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | no | — |
| `maxIterations` | integer | no | `5` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Repeats the nodes connected to its 'loop' output once per item, then continues from its 'done' output. Iterates the incoming array, or the configured items, up to maxIterations. The number of iterations is always bounded.

</details>

### `core.delay` — Delay

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Pauses the run for a while, then carries on with exactly what it was given. A short delay — ten seconds or less — waits in place; a longer one puts the run to sleep as Waiting and wakes it at the right time, so a run can wait minutes, hours or up to 30 days without holding anything open.

**Input.** anything — it is passed through untouched.

**Output.** its input, unchanged.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number | no | `1` |
| `unit` | `milliseconds` · `seconds` · `minutes` · `hours` · `days` | no | `seconds` |

**Examples**

- *Space out calls to a rate-limited API* — { "amount": 2, "unit": "seconds" }
- *Send a follow-up a day later* — { "amount": 1, "unit": "days" }

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Waits, then passes its input through unchanged. Waits over 10 seconds pause the run and resume it later, up to 30 days. Use it to space out calls to a rate-limited service, or to wait before a follow-up.

</details>

### `core.approval` — Approval

**branch** · **not** callable by the agent

Stops the run and asks a person to approve or reject, then carries on down Approved or Rejected — hours or days later. Connect Ask to a Discord, Slack or Gmail step to send the decision link ({{input.url}}); whoever opens it can decide without signing in, once. It is also waiting in the inbox and on the canvas for the people allowed to decide. If nobody does before the timeout, On timeout decides.

**Input.** anything — what it was given is what the message's {{input.…}} references read

**Output.** Ask: { url, message, expiresAt, approvalId }. Approved and Rejected: { decision, via, decidedBy: { name, email } or null, comment, decidedAt, message }.

**Branches.** Ask (`ask`) · Approved (`approved`) · Rejected (`rejected`)

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | yes | — |
| `approvers` | string | no | — |
| `timeout` | number | no | `1` |
| `timeoutUnit` | `minutes` · `hours` · `days` | no | `days` |
| `onTimeout` | `reject` · `approve` · `fail` | no | `reject` |

**Examples**

- *The message* — "Refund {{input.amount}} to {{input.customer}}?"
- *Send the link to Discord, from Ask* — "Approval needed: {{input.message}} — {{input.url}}"
- *Only named people decide* — { "approvers": "ada@example.com, grace@example.com" }
- *On Approved, use the comment* — "Approved by {{input.decidedBy.name}}: {{input.comment}}"

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Pauses the run until a person approves or rejects, for up to 30 days. Ask fires at once with {{input.url}}, the decision link: connect it to the Discord, Slack or Gmail step that sends it. Approved and Rejected continue after the decision.

</details>

### `core.call_workflow` — Call workflow

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Runs another workflow in this workspace as part of this one, waits for it to finish, and carries on with what it returned. The other workflow starts at its own trigger, with Input as its payload; its run appears on its own page, linked to this one. It cannot pause or ask a person, and workflows cannot call one another in a circle or more than three deep.

**Input.** anything — handed to the called workflow as its payload unless Input says otherwise

**Output.** { output: what the called workflow's last step produced, runId: the called run's id, workflowId, workflow: its name }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflowId` | string | yes | — |
| `input` | any | no | — |

**Examples**

- *Use what it returned* — {{input.output.total}}
- *Pass a mapped Input* — { "email": "{{input.email}}", "plan": "pro" }
- *Open the called run* — {{input.runId}}

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Runs another workflow from this workspace and waits for it, then outputs what that workflow finished with. Pass it data with Input; it defaults to what this step received. A called workflow cannot wait or ask a person.

</details>

### `core.merge` — Merge

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Where branches that ran side by side meet again. In All mode it waits until every branch still on its way has reached it and then runs once, with what each carried; in First mode it runs on the first branch and ignores the rest. Without a Merge, a step that two branches lead to runs twice.

**Input.** the branches leading into it — it reads them itself and hands on one combined value

**Output.** { count: how many branches were joined, inputs: [one value per branch in the order they reached it], from: [the id of the node each came from] }. Read one branch as {{input.inputs[0].field}}.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `all` · `first` | no | `all` |

**Examples**

- *Read the first branch's field* — {{input.inputs[0].title}}
- *How many were joined* — {{input.count}}
- *Which node a branch came from* — {{input.from[1]}}
- *A branch's output by node id, from anywhere after the merge* — {{steps.fetch_weather.output.temp}}

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Joins branches that run side by side and runs once. In all mode it waits until every branch still on its way has reached it; in first mode it runs on the first branch and ignores the rest. Outputs how many were joined and what each carried.

</details>

### `core.respond` — Respond

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Decides what the caller of this workflow is told: a status code, a JSON body made from your data, and a few allowed headers. Without one the caller gets a summary of the run, as before. Only the first Respond to run counts, and it only matters when a request from outside started the run.

**Input.** nothing in particular — reference any earlier step with {{steps.<id>.output.x}}

**Output.** { status, headers, body } — the reply that was set.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | integer | no | `200` |
| `body` | object | no | `{}` |
| `headers` | object | no | `{}` |

**Examples**

- *A look-up result* — status 200 · body { "price": "{{steps.fetch.output.price}}" }
- *Refuse a caller* — status 422 · body { "error": "That order does not exist" }
- *Tell a client to retry* — status 503 · headers retry-after: 30

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Sets the reply the caller of this workflow gets back: a status code, a JSON body and headers. Use it when the caller needs data back, not just an acknowledgement.

</details>

### `core.assert` — Assert

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Fails the run when the condition is false, with the message you configure. Use it to stop a workflow early when incoming data is not what it must be.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `left` | any | yes | — |
| `operator` | `equals` · `not_equals` · `contains` · `greater_than` · `less_than` · `is_empty` · `is_not_empty` | no | `is_not_empty` |
| `right` | any | no | — |
| `message` | string | no | `Assertion failed.` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Fails the run when the condition is false, with the message you configure. Use it to stop a workflow early when incoming data is not what it must be.

</details>

## Transform

Pure data shaping. None of them reach the network, and each one reads the previous node's list, so they chain with nothing in between.

### `core.set` — Set data

**action** · callable by the agent

Produces a JSON object from the fields you configure. Field values may reference earlier data with {{input.x}} or {{steps.<nodeId>.output.y}}. Use it to reshape or enrich data between nodes.

**Output.** the object you configured in `fields`, merged over the incoming input when `merge` is true. Reference a field directly, e.g. output.subject.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | object | no | `{}` |
| `merge` | boolean | no | `false` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Produces a JSON object from the fields you configure. Field values may reference earlier data with {{input.x}} or {{steps.<nodeId>.output.y}}. Use it to reshape or enrich data between nodes.

</details>

### `transform.filter` — Filter list

**action** · callable by the agent

Narrows a list down to the items you care about. Every item is tested the same way a Branch node tests a single value, so the operators behave identically — what this adds is the ability to look at a property inside each item.

**Input.** A list — either the previous node's output when that is a list, or its `items` property when it is one of the other list nodes.

**Output.** { items: the items that passed, count: how many passed, removed: how many were dropped, total: how many came in }. Use output.items to pass the list on.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | no | — |
| `field` | string | no | `""` |
| `operator` | `equals` · `not_equals` · `contains` · `greater_than` · `less_than` · `is_empty` · `is_not_empty` | no | `equals` |
| `value` | any | no | — |

**Examples**

- *Only the open issues* — field: state · operator: equals · value: open
- *Rows that actually have an email* — field: user.email · operator: is_not_empty
- *Scores above the bar* — field: score · operator: greater_than · value: 80

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Keeps only the items of a list that pass a test, and drops the rest. Set field to a property inside each item (for example 'status' or 'user.email') or leave it empty to test each item itself. Reads the incoming list, or the items you configure.

</details>

### `transform.map` — Reshape list

**action** · callable by the agent

Turns a list of one shape into a list of another. Name the keys you want out and, for each, the path to read it from inside the item. Anything a path does not find comes out as null rather than missing, so every item has the same keys.

**Input.** A list — the previous node's output, or its `items` property.

**Output.** { items: the rebuilt objects, count: how many }. Each item has exactly the keys named in fields.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | no | — |
| `fields` | object | no | `{}` |

**Examples**

- *Flatten a nested API response* — fields: { "name": "user.name", "email": "user.email", "id": "id" }
- *Keep two columns for a spreadsheet* — fields: { "title": "title", "url": "html_url" }

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Rebuilds every item of a list into a new object with the fields you name. Each field's value is a path inside the item, such as 'name' or 'user.email'. Use it to flatten or rename data before sending it somewhere else.

</details>

### `transform.sort` — Sort list

**action** · callable by the agent

Puts a list in order. Values that look like numbers are compared as numbers, so 10 comes after 9 rather than before it. Items missing the field sort to the end, which keeps a half-populated list readable.

**Input.** A list — the previous node's output, or its `items` property.

**Output.** { items: the list in order, count: how many }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | no | — |
| `field` | string | no | `""` |
| `direction` | `asc` · `desc` | no | `asc` |

**Examples**

- *Highest score first* — field: score · direction: desc
- *Oldest first* — field: created_at · direction: asc
- *Plain strings, A–Z* — field: (empty) · direction: asc

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Orders a list. Set field to a property inside each item, such as 'score' or 'created_at', or leave it empty to sort the items themselves. Numbers sort numerically and text sorts alphabetically.

</details>

### `transform.unique` — Remove duplicates

**action** · callable by the agent

Keeps the first occurrence of each distinct item and drops the rest. Whole objects are compared by their contents, not by identity, so two separately built objects with the same fields count as duplicates.

**Input.** A list — the previous node's output, or its `items` property.

**Output.** { items: the list with repeats removed, count: how many remain, removed: how many were dropped, total: how many came in }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | no | — |
| `field` | string | no | `""` |

**Examples**

- *One row per person* — field: email
- *Distinct tags* — field: (empty)

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Removes repeated items from a list, keeping the first of each. Set field to compare a property inside each item, such as 'email', or leave it empty to compare whole items.

</details>

### `transform.aggregate` — Summarise list

**action** · callable by the agent

Turns a whole list into a single number or string — how many, how much, the biggest, or everything joined into one line of text. Non-numeric entries are skipped by the arithmetic operations rather than counted as zero, and the output says how many were skipped.

**Input.** A list — the previous node's output, or its `items` property.

**Output.** { value: the result, operation, count: how many items came in, skipped: how many were ignored because they were not numbers }. Use output.value.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array | no | — |
| `operation` | `count` · `sum` · `average` · `min` · `max` · `join` · `first` · `last` | no | `count` |
| `field` | string | no | `""` |
| `separator` | string | no | `, ` |

**Examples**

- *Total revenue* — operation: sum · field: amount
- *How many open issues* — operation: count
- *One line for a Discord message* — operation: join · field: title · separator: ", "

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Reduces a list to one value: count, sum, average, min, max, join, first or last. Set field to a property inside each item, such as 'amount', or leave it empty to use the items themselves.

</details>

### `transform.json` — JSON

**action** · callable by the agent

Moves data across the line between text and structure. Parse turns a string of JSON into something the rest of the workflow can reference into; stringify does the reverse for a node that wants text.

**Input.** The previous node's output when `value` is not configured — a string for parse, anything for stringify.

**Output.** parse: { value: the parsed data, type: 'object' | 'array' | 'string' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'null' }. stringify: { text: the JSON text, length }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `parse` · `stringify` | no | `parse` |
| `value` | any | no | — |
| `pretty` | boolean | no | `false` |

**Examples**

- *An API that returned text/plain* — mode: parse · value: {{steps.fetch.output.body}}
- *A JSON body for an HTTP request* — mode: stringify · pretty: false

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Converts between JSON text and data. Use parse when a previous node handed you a string that contains JSON, and stringify when something downstream needs the data as text.

</details>

### `transform.text` — Edit text

**action** · callable by the agent

One node for the small text jobs that sit between two other nodes — tidying a value before it is compared, cutting a subject line down to size, or splitting a comma-separated field into a real list.

**Input.** The previous node's output as text, when `text` is not configured.

**Output.** { text: the result, length } for every operation except split, which gives { items: the pieces, count }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | no | — |
| `operation` | `trim` · `lowercase` · `uppercase` · `title_case` · `replace` · `split` · `slice` · `prepend` · `append` | no | `trim` |
| `search` | string | no | `""` |
| `value` | string | no | `""` |
| `start` | integer | no | `0` |
| `end` | integer | no | — |

**Examples**

- *Tidy a value before comparing it* — operation: trim, then lowercase
- *Split "a, b, c" into a list* — operation: split · separator: ", "
- *Cut a subject line to 80 characters* — operation: slice · start: 0 · end: 80
- *Label a Discord message* — operation: prepend · value: "Daily report: "

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Changes a piece of text: trim, change case, replace a substring, split it into a list, cut a section out, or add something to the front or back. Replacement is literal text, not a pattern.

</details>

### `transform.number` — Do maths

**action** · callable by the agent

One arithmetic step. Useful for turning a raw count into something worth saying — a percentage, a rounded average, a running total added to an earlier one.

**Input.** The previous node's output as a number, when `value` is not configured.

**Output.** { value: the result, operation }. Use output.value.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | any | no | — |
| `operation` | `add` · `subtract` · `multiply` · `divide` · `round` · `floor` · `ceil` · `absolute` · `percent_of` | no | `add` |
| `operand` | any | no | — |
| `precision` | integer | no | — |

**Examples**

- *Round an average to a whole number* — value: {{steps.avg.output.value}} · operation: round
- *What share passed* — value: {{steps.passed.output.count}} · operation: percent_of · operand: {{steps.all.output.count}}
- *Add VAT* — operation: multiply · operand: 1.2 · precision: 2

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Performs one arithmetic operation on a number: add, subtract, multiply, divide, round, floor, ceil, absolute value, or what percentage one number is of another. Both values may reference earlier data.

</details>

### `transform.date` — Date and time

**action** · callable by the agent

Gives you the current time, or reformats one you already have, in every shape a downstream node is likely to want. Time zone is explicit and defaults to UTC, because the server this runs on is not in your time zone.

**Input.** The previous node's output as a date string, when `value` is not configured.

**Output.** { iso, date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', time: 'HH:MM:SS', unix: seconds, year, month, day, hour, minute, weekday: 'Monday', monthName: 'January', timeZone }. Pick the one you need, e.g. output.date.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | any | no | — |
| `shiftMinutes` | integer | no | `0` |
| `timeZone` | string | no | `UTC` |

**Examples**

- *Today's date for a report title* — → {{steps.date.output.date}}
- *Yesterday, in Singapore* — shiftMinutes: -1440 · timeZone: Asia/Singapore
- *A timestamp for a spreadsheet row* — → {{steps.date.output.iso}}

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Produces a point in time in several formats at once — ISO, date only, time only, Unix seconds, and the parts. Defaults to now. Set value to read an existing date, and shiftMinutes to move it forward or back.

</details>

---

## Agent

The reasoning nodes. `ai.llm` asks a model once; `ai.agent` loops — thinking, calling other nodes as tools, and deciding when it is done.

### `ai.llm` — LLM

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Sends a prompt to the configured language model and outputs its answer as text. Use it to summarise, rewrite, classify or extract from data produced earlier in the workflow.

**Output.** { text: the model's answer as a string, json: the parsed answer when json is true else null, model, usage, input }. To use the answer, reference output.text — output on its own is the whole object.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prompt` | string | yes | — |
| `system` | string | no | — |
| `model` | string | no | — |
| `temperature` | number | no | — |
| `json` | boolean | no | `false` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Sends a prompt to the configured language model and outputs its answer as text. Use it to summarise, rewrite, classify or extract from data produced earlier in the workflow.

</details>

### `ai.agent` — AI Agent

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Gives an objective to a language model that can call other nodes as tools and decide what to do at runtime. Outputs its answer, the decision it reached, and every tool call it made.

**Output.** { decision: one of the configured choices, or null, reason: one sentence explaining it, text: the full answer, toolCalls, iterations, model, usage, input }. Route on output.decision.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objective` | string | yes | — |
| `system` | string | no | — |
| `model` | string | no | — |
| `tools` | array of string | no | `[]` |
| `choices` | array of string | no | `[]` |
| `maxIterations` | integer | no | `5` |
| `temperature` | number | no | — |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Gives an objective to a language model that can call other nodes as tools and decide what to do at runtime. Outputs its answer, the decision it reached, and every tool call it made.

</details>

---

## Integration

The nodes that reach a real service. Each one is bound to a credential you created, which is what fixes its destination.

### `integration.http` — HTTP request

**action** · callable by the agent

Calls an HTTPS API and outputs its response. Use it to fetch or send data to any web service that is not covered by a dedicated node. The URL must be https and must be a public address; redirects are reported rather than followed.

**Output.** { status: the HTTP status number, ok: true for 2xx, json: the parsed response body or null, text: the raw response body, contentType, redirectedTo }. For a JSON API, reference output.json.field.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `GET` · `POST` · `PUT` · `PATCH` · `DELETE` | no | `GET` |
| `url` | string | yes | — |
| `headers` | object | no | — |
| `body` | string | no | — |
| `timeoutMs` | integer | no | `15000` |
| `failOnError` | boolean | no | `true` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Calls an HTTPS API and outputs its response. Use it to fetch or send data to any web service that is not covered by a dedicated node. The URL must be https and must be a public address; redirects are reported rather than followed.

</details>

### `integration.discord` — Post to Discord

**action** · callable by the agent

Posts a message to the Discord channel the user has connected in Settings. Use it to notify people about something the workflow found. The channel is fixed by the stored credential; only the message text is chosen here.

**Output.** { posted: true, messageId: the id Discord created, channelId, content: the message that was sent }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | string | yes | — |
| `username` | string | no | — |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Posts a message to the Discord channel the user has connected in Settings. Use it to notify people about something the workflow found. The channel is fixed by the stored credential; only the message text is chosen here.

</details>

### `integration.slack` — Post to Slack

**action** · callable by the agent

Sends one message to a single Slack channel — the one you chose when you created the incoming webhook in Settings → Integrations. It is the quickest way to make a workflow tell a human something, and it is the node to reach for when a run should end in somebody being told.

**Input.** Nothing in particular. It ignores its input and sends the text you write, so put `{{ }}` references in the message to pull values out of earlier steps.

**Output.** { posted: true, text: the message that was sent }. Slack answers an incoming webhook with no message id, so there is nothing else to report.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | — |

**Examples**

- *Report what an earlier step found* — text: "{{steps.summarise.output.text}}"
- *Announce a webhook that arrived* — text: "New signup: {{trigger.email}} on the {{trigger.plan}} plan"

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Posts a message to the Slack channel the user has connected in Settings. Use it to tell people about something the workflow found or did. The channel is fixed by the stored webhook; only the message text is chosen here.

</details>

### `integration.sheets` — Append to Google Sheet

**action** · callable by the agent

Appends one row to a Google Sheet using the user's connected Google account. Use it to record something the workflow produced. Give the spreadsheet id (or its URL), the sheet tab name, and the row's cells in order.

**Output.** { appended: true, spreadsheetId, updatedRange: where the row landed e.g. Sheet1!A7:E7, updatedRows, values: the row that was written }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheetId` | string | no | `""` |
| `sheet` | string | no | `Sheet1` |
| `values` | array | yes | — |
| `valueInputOption` | `USER_ENTERED` · `RAW` | no | `RAW` |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Appends one row to a Google Sheet using the user's connected Google account. Use it to record something the workflow produced. Give the spreadsheet id (or its URL), the sheet tab name, and the row's cells in order.

</details>

### `integration.gmail` — Send email

**action** · **not** callable by the agent

Sends an email from the user's connected Gmail account. Use it to deliver a result to a person by mail.

**Output.** { sent: true, messageId, threadId, to, subject }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | string | no | `""` |
| `subject` | string | no | `""` |
| `body` | string | no | `""` |
| `cc` | string | no | — |

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Sends an email from the user's connected Gmail account. Use it to deliver a result to a person by mail.

</details>

### `integration.notion` — Write to Notion

**action** · callable by the agent

Records something in Notion, either by adding paragraphs to the bottom of a page you already have or by creating a new page inside a database — which is how a Notion database gets a new row. Useful as the last step of a workflow that should leave a written trail somebody can read later.

**Input.** Nothing in particular; it writes the title and body you configure. Use `{{ }}` references to pull in text an earlier step produced.

**Output.** { operation, pageId: the page appended to or created, url: its Notion link when Notion returns one, blocks: how many paragraphs were written }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `appendToPage` · `addDatabaseRow` | no | `appendToPage` |
| `target` | string | no | `""` |
| `title` | string | no | `""` |
| `titleProperty` | string | no | `Name` |
| `body` | string | no | `""` |

**Examples**

- *Append a run's findings to a log page* — operation: appendToPage · target: the page link · body: "{{steps.summarise.output.text}}"
- *Add a row to a task database* — operation: addDatabaseRow · target: the database link · title: "{{trigger.subject}}" · titleProperty: Name

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Writes to Notion using the workspace's connected integration. With operation "appendToPage" it adds paragraphs to the end of an existing page; with "addDatabaseRow" it creates a new page in a database, which is what adding a row means in Notion. Give target as the page or database id, or paste its Notion link.

</details>

### `integration.github` — GitHub issue

**action** · callable by the agent

Turns something a workflow found into a GitHub issue, or adds a comment to an issue that already exists. Good for putting a failure, a support request or a scheduled review somewhere a team already looks, rather than in a chat message that scrolls away.

**Input.** Nothing in particular. Write the title and body yourself, using `{{ }}` references for anything an earlier step produced.

**Output.** { operation, repo: owner/name, number: the issue number, url: the link to the issue or the comment }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `createIssue` · `commentOnIssue` | no | `createIssue` |
| `repo` | string | no | `""` |
| `title` | string | no | `""` |
| `body` | string | no | `""` |
| `issueNumber` | integer | no | — |
| `labels` | array of string | no | `[]` |

**Examples**

- *File what a webhook reported* — operation: createIssue · repo: acme/api · title: "{{trigger.subject}}" · labels: ["bug"]
- *Comment on the issue a previous step opened* — operation: commentOnIssue · repo: acme/api · issueNumber: {{steps.file.output.number}} · body: "Run finished."

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Files a GitHub issue, or comments on an existing one, using the workspace's connected token. Operation "createIssue" needs repo and title; "commentOnIssue" needs repo, issueNumber and body. Give repo as owner/name. It can only reach the repositories the stored token was granted, and it never changes code.

</details>

### `integration.airtable` — Airtable record

**action** · callable by the agent

Uses an Airtable base as a workflow's memory — write a row when something happens, or read a page of rows to work through. In list mode it returns items and count like every other list node, so a filter or a sort can follow it directly with nothing in between.

**Input.** Nothing in particular. In createRecord mode the fields object is what gets written, and every key must match an Airtable column name exactly, capitals included.

**Output.** After createRecord: { operation, recordId, fields: the row as Airtable stored it }. After listRecords: { operation, items: one object per row with its id, createdTime and fields, count }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `createRecord` · `listRecords` | no | `createRecord` |
| `baseId` | string | no | `""` |
| `table` | string | no | `""` |
| `fields` | object | no | — |
| `maxRecords` | integer | no | `20` |
| `view` | string | no | `""` |
| `typecast` | boolean | no | `true` |

**Examples**

- *Log a webhook into a base* — operation: createRecord · fields: { "Name": "{{trigger.name}}", "Email": "{{trigger.email}}" }
- *Read rows, then narrow them* — operation: listRecords · maxRecords: 50, then a Filter node on field "fields.Status"

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Reads or writes Airtable records using the workspace's connected token. Operation "createRecord" adds one row from the fields given; "listRecords" returns a page of rows as items. Give baseId (it starts with app) and the exact table name. It can only reach the bases the stored token was granted.

</details>

### `integration.postgres` — Postgres query

**action** · callable by the agent

Reads from a Postgres database you have connected, and cannot write to it. Rows come back as items with the column names as keys, so a Filter, Sort or Aggregate node chains straight on. Use count when you want the total rather than the rows — it asks the server, so it is not capped by the limit.

**Input.** Nothing in particular. Everything it needs is in its own configuration, so it works as the first step after a trigger.

**Output.** After select: { operation, table, items: one object per row keyed by column name, count: how many rows came back }. After count: { operation, table, items: [], count: the total number of matching rows }.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | `select` · `count` | no | `select` |
| `schema` | string | no | `public` |
| `table` | string | no | `""` |
| `columns` | array of string | no | `[]` |
| `where` | array of object | no | `[]` |
| `orderBy` | string | no | `""` |
| `direction` | `asc` · `desc` | no | `asc` |
| `limit` | integer | no | `50` |
| `timeoutMs` | integer | no | `10000` |

**Examples**

- *The ten largest cities* — table: city · orderBy: population · direction: desc · limit: 10
- *Narrow it with a where list* — where: [{ "column": "country", "operator": "equals", "value": "IN" }]
- *How many rows match* — operation: count · where: [{ "column": "notes", "operator": "is_not_empty" }]

<details><summary>What the agent reads</summary>

> Reads rows from the workspace's connected Postgres database. Give it schema (usually public), table, and optionally columns, a where list and an order. Operation "select" returns the matching rows as items; "count" returns only how many match, which is the one to use when the answer is a number. It can never write — every query runs in a read-only transaction. There is no SQL field; build the query from these parts.

</details>

## Why some nodes are not agent tools

`agentCallable` defaults to `false`. Widening what an agent may reach is a deliberate act per
node, never a side effect of registering one — see [`agents.md`](./agents.md) and
[`../SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md) → *The agent, and what it cannot reach*.

| Node | Why not |
|---|---|
| `core.manual_trigger` | A trigger starts a run; an agent runs inside one. |
| `core.webhook_trigger` | A trigger starts a run; an agent runs inside one. |
| `core.schedule_trigger` | A trigger starts a run; an agent runs inside one. |
| `core.error_trigger` | A trigger starts a run; an agent runs inside one. |
| `core.form_trigger` | A trigger starts a run; an agent runs inside one. |
| `core.branch` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.switch` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.loop` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.delay` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.approval` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.call_workflow` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.merge` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.respond` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `core.assert` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `ai.llm` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `ai.agent` | Flow control belongs to the graph, not to a tool call. |
| `integration.gmail` | Sends mail as you. A model deciding to send email is a blast radius, not a feature. |
